metaData.originalTitle: 一部「黑」奥特曼的电影，被 OpenAI 金主连夜雪藏
metaData.title: A Film Smearing Altman, Shelved Overnight by OpenAI's Biggest Backer
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Amazon MGM pulled the film 'Artificial' about OpenAI's internal strife, due to Amazon's huge cooperation with OpenAI, making the film's negative portrayal of Altman a commercial risk, reflecting the invisible intervention of tech capital on narratives.
metaData.summary: The article reports that Amazon-owned MGM Studios has ceased distribution of Luca Guadagnino's film 'Artificial', which centers on the 2023 OpenAI boardroom drama, portraying Sam Altman as a "liar and schemer" while depicting Ilya Sutskever as an idealistic tech genius. The film is mostly shot, boasts a star-studded team, and was originally slated for awards season. Amazon offered vague reasons for shelving it, but the article points to a key background: Amazon has invested USD 50 billion in OpenAI and signed a cloud service deal worth hundreds of billions, becoming one of its biggest backers. The article delves into the commercial logic behind the shelving—a film that offends a strategic partner turns from "asset" to "risk"; it also explores whether stories about tech giants can be freely told when those giants deeply penetrate the entertainment industry. Currently, no distributor dares to pick up the film, and it may be shelved indefinitely, becoming a classic case of power intervening in narratives through capital rather than outright censorship.

mainPoints.point: The direct reason Amazon MGM shelved 'Artificial' is a conflict of commercial interests.
mainPoints.explanation: Amazon first became OpenAI's cloud service provider, then invested USD 50 billion and added a cloud deal worth hundreds of billions. The film portrays Altman negatively, so releasing it would offend this newly strategic partner, leading to its abandonment.

mainPoints.point: The film tells the story of OpenAI's boardroom drama as a tale of an idealist defeated by a schemer.
mainPoints.explanation: The script portrays Ilya Sutskever as the true idealistic genius behind the core technology, Altman as a calculating liar, and Elon Musk as a villain and comic relief. This narrative orientation is the core of the controversy.

mainPoints.point: No public ban is needed for shelving; the logic of capital automatically takes effect.
mainPoints.explanation: No one issued an order to suppress it, but as long as the film is considered a 'risk', distributors naturally back away. Other buyers are also deterred by the fear of offending tech giants, demonstrating the invisible intervention of power over narratives.

keyQuotes: No distributor would be willing to offend a tech mogul who might become their benefactor or partner at any moment, just for the sake of one film.
The truly efficient kind is often much quieter: it says nothing, doesn't even make a move, but merely existing can make a film that the entire crew poured their hearts into vanish into thin air.

relatedArticles.title: Technology Enthusiast Weekly (Issue 401): How to Make 1 Billion Dollars
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article excerpts Paul Graham's speech on how to make 1 billion dollars through entrepreneurship, with the core message being to maintain a high growth rate and enter a large market, supplemented by growth calculation examples and other tech news.

relatedArticles.title: Most Companies Are Not Ready for AI
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: The fundamental reason most companies fail to effectively leverage AI is not technological immaturity, but their own strategic ambiguity, unclear goals, and chaotic processes, which prevent them from providing clear and precise instructions to AI.

relatedArticles.title: "The Biggest IPO in Human History": Is SpaceX More Than Just Rockets?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on SpaceX's prospectus, this article analyzes its $45 billion computing contract with Anthropic, its holdings of 18,712 Bitcoin, its board composition and aggressive governance structure, and the critical significance of the V3 Starship test flight for its valuation.

relatedArticles.title: Is WeChat the First to Bring an AI OS to 1.4 Billion People?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article analyzes WeChat's latest AI ecosystem integration guidelines, pointing out that through its mini-program centralized architecture, it allows AI to directly operate millions of third-party services, bringing it closer to the form of an 'AI OS' than Apple's Siri.

relatedArticles.title: The First Batch of Agent Employees Are Onboard: Tencent Cloud Wants to Help Enterprises Settle Them In
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: At its annual conference, Tencent Cloud released a series of Agent products and infrastructure, aiming to upgrade AI from a tool to an integral part of enterprise production systems, with a core strategy centered on building an enterprise-grade Agent operating system around scenario connectivity, engineering mastery, and model driving force.

relatedArticles.title: Codex and Claude Code Leads No Longer Write Prompts — What Exactly Is the Loop Taking the AI World by Storm?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explains the paradigm shift in AI coding from Prompt Engineering to Loop Engineering, detailing the core concepts, components, applicable scenarios, and real-world barriers of the loop.

relatedArticles.title: Just Now: Major Codex Update — Your Computer Operations Are Becoming AI's Training Data
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI Codex launches Record & Replay, allowing users to record computer operations and convert them into reusable AI skills, marking a shift from AI relying on APIs to directly learning how humans use graphical interfaces.

relatedArticles.title: Dialogue with MiniMax's Zeyin: Agents Will Eventually Surpass Humans, Where Do We Go From Here?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Through an in-depth conversation with Zeyin, an Agent R&D engineer at MiniMax, this article reveals the design philosophy and technical details of the Agent Team architecture (Leader-Worker-Verifier), as well as the current consensus and trend in the AI Agent industry shifting from model competition to harness competition.

relatedArticles.title: iPhone Finally Gets Siri AI! But Mainland China Misses Out on the First Release, Alarm Clock Becomes the Biggest Surprise
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: WWDC26 unveils iOS 27 and new Apple Intelligence developments, upgrading Siri to a system-level AI assistant with its own app, but users in mainland China will temporarily miss out on the AI features.

relatedArticles.title: A Comprehensive Guide to Microsoft Build 2026: The 'Agent-First' Era Arrives with Seven In-House Models
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Microsoft Build 2026 unveiled seven in-house MAI models, the Scout agent, the MXC system-level security sandbox, and Project Solara, marking the full implementation of an 'Agent-First' strategy.
